faq_q1: How will I receive the book or pattern after purchase?
faq_a1: It depends on the version you choose. With an Amazon purchase you will receive a printed book — delivery time and location depend on the chosen shipping method. With a PDF purchase the file is available immediately after buying — you will receive a download link by email.
faq_q2: Can I print the purchased PDF?
faq_a2: Yes, PDF files are intended for personal printing. You may print as many copies as you need for your own use.
faq_q3: Are the books available in Polish?
faq_a3: Most books and all patterns are in Polish. Some books are published in English — those editions are marked 🇬🇧, and every card carries a badge showing the product's language.
faq_q4: What is the difference between the Amazon and PDF versions?
faq_a4: The Amazon version is a printed book delivered by post. The PDF version is a digital file to download and print at home — available immediately after purchase, with no shipping costs.
faq_q5: Are the patterns suitable for beginners?
faq_a5: Each publication has a marked difficulty level. Some projects are for beginners, others for intermediate knitters — check the description of each book.
faq_q6: Can I return a PDF I bought?
faq_a6: PDF files purchased via Payhip are non-refundable once downloaded, as they are digital products. If a file won’t open or is damaged, write to us and we’ll help.
pfaq_q1: What does each PDF pattern include?
pfaq_a1: Each pattern includes a chart with a symbol grid, a legend (PL + EN), instructions on reading the chart, yarn and needle recommendations, and practical tips.
pfaq_a2: Patterns are marked with a difficulty level. The current lace patterns (Lace Leaf, Powder Leaf) are for intermediate knitters who know the basics of knitting and reading charts.
pfaq_q3: How do I get the file after purchase?
pfaq_a3: Right after purchase you will receive an email with a link to download the PDF file. The file is also available in your Payhip account.
pfaq_q4: Can I use a pattern commercially?
pfaq_a4: The patterns are for personal use only. Copying, reselling or commercial use of the charts is not permitted.
pfaq_q5: What yarn is recommended for lace patterns?
pfaq_a5: Lace patterns work best with DK or sport weight yarn in light, solid colours (cotton, linen, merino, silk). Blocking is essential — it fully opens up the lace.
pfaq_q6: Can I return a PDF pattern I bought?
pfaq_a6: PDF patterns purchased via Payhip are non-refundable once downloaded, as they are digital products. If a file won’t open or is damaged, write to us and we’ll help.

wzorai_tagline: Your assistant for creative knitting patterns
wzorai_hero_sub: Describe a pattern in your own words — get a ready-to-knit chart
wzorai_intro: Every knitter knows the feeling: you can picture the fabric exactly — the way the lace opens, where the cable crosses — but that pattern is in no book and on no forum. WzorAI starts from your words. Write ‘lace diamonds on a purl ground’ or ‘a cable with seed stitch on either side’ — and the app builds the repeat, checks that every row adds up, and draws a clear chart in the symbols you know.
wzorai_how1_d: In plain language, the way you would tell a friend. If you are short of an idea, open the idea builder: tap a few words — lace, leaves, airy, for a scarf — and the description writes itself.
wzorai_how2_d: It builds the repeat and checks it row by row: does the stitch count work out, do the yarn-overs balance the decreases. A chart that cannot be knitted never reaches your screen.
wzorai_how3_d: From your phone with zoom and a row counter, or from a printed PDF beside your needles. Whichever suits you.
wzorai_f1_d: Every pattern goes through an automatic check. If a row does not balance, the app corrects the pattern and checks again — until it works.
wzorai_f2_d: One tap switches the view to fabric: the pattern repeated nine times, with fine gold lines at the repeat boundaries. Only here does the motif reveal itself.
wzorai_f3_d: Tap a row and it lights up. Close the app, come back a week later — your place is waiting where you left it.
wzorai_f4_d: Cast-on, shaping for sleeves and necklines, and how much yarn — worked out from the weight of your own swatch, not from a table.
wzorai_f5_d: Seven pages: cover, chart, fabric preview, legend, row-by-row instructions, care and blocking. All in your language, ready to print.
wzorai_f6_d: The history stays on your device. Name patterns your own way, star the favourites, and add notes. Six months on you will still know what the project was.
wzorai_f7_d: Chart and legend in one picture — to send to a friend or post on Instagram.
wzorai_f8_d: Fifty practical tips and facts about knitting — from keeping your ball of yarn from rolling away, to why mohair unravels better after an hour in the freezer.
wzorai_who_d: For anyone who knits and wants a pattern they will not find anywhere else. Skill level does not matter: every chart is marked with a difficulty, and eight built-in examples can be viewed and exported free of charge before you decide on anything.
wzorai_det_lang: Languages: English, Polish, German, French, Russian, Ukrainian — the whole app and every PDF.
wzorai_det_sym: Symbols: European or international (CYC) standard, your choice in settings.
wzorai_det_priv: Privacy: no registration, no account, no personal details. Your charts are stored on your device only.
wzorai_det_pay: Payment: no subscription. You buy a pack of patterns — 5, 20 or 50 — and use them at your own pace. If a generation fails, the pattern is not counted.
wzorai_ai_d: WzorAI uses artificial intelligence, and we say so plainly. That is exactly why every chart goes through a mathematical check, and why each pattern carries the reminder that holds for any pattern anyway: knit a small swatch first. It is the surest way to see how the motif behaves in your yarn.

shift_hero_sub: 4:10 a.m. The alarm rings — and it’s the right one.
shift_intro: Your rota hangs on the wall at work or arrives as a blurry photo in a group chat. Every month it’s the same: copy it into your phone, set the alarms one by one, check it all again… and one mistake is enough to oversleep an early shift or turn up on your day off. ShiftLens does it for you: take a photo of the rota, and a minute later every shift of the month has its own alarm.
shift_how1_d: The whole sheet — an on-screen frame helps you fit it in, and you can crop the corners afterwards. Excel and PDF files work too.
shift_how2_d: Exactly as it is printed. ShiftLens finds your row even in a rota for the whole team.
shift_how3_d: Days the app was not sure about are clearly marked. You fix them with a single tap.
shift_how4_d: Alarms set for the whole month — and the app reads the month itself from the sheet.
shift_f1_t: An alarm that fits the shift
shift_f1_d: For a 6:00 shift it wakes you earlier, for a 14:00 shift later. Getting-ready and travel time are set separately for morning, afternoon and night shifts.
shift_f2_d: They come back after a phone restart. If the phone switches them off, the app warns you and shows exactly what to change. Test the ring with one tap.
shift_f3_t: A nudge before the rota ends
shift_f3_d: Three days before your last shift you are reminded that the rota is running out. Your own alarm sound and extra alarms whenever you need them.
shift_f4_d: A whole-team table, a “date – shift” list, several pages at once, plus Excel and PDF files. Any day can be fixed by hand, and a missing one simply added.
shift_f5_d: Days off, holidays and sick leave — in words or letters: “Wolne”, “Urlop”, “Urlaub”, “Folga” or just “U” in a cell.
shift_f6_d: Two rotas side by side, each with its company name and colour. The alarm before your second shift never rings before the first one ends. Changing jobs? The new one takes over the rota from a date you choose.
shift_f7_d: Monthly total with the unpaid break deducted, separately for each job. Overtime shown next to rota hours, plus a history of past months.
shift_f8_d: A home-screen widget in three sizes counts down to your next shift — and, during it, to the end. Send the rota to your family as a clear image.
shift_who_d: Shops, warehouses, factories, restaurants, hospitals, security, logistics — for anyone who gets their rota on paper and starts work at a different time every day.
shift_det_lang: Languages: Polish, English, Ukrainian, Russian, German, French, Spanish, Portuguese.
shift_det_net: Internet: not needed — the app works offline.
shift_det_ads: Payment: one-time purchase, no subscription and no ads.
shift_priv_title: Your rota stays on your phone
shift_priv_d: Text recognition runs on the device. Photos and rotas are never sent anywhere, no account is needed, and the app works offline. Colleagues’ names are deleted right after reading — only your own shifts are saved.
